narrative.overview: Wisphive is an instrument panel, not an app. The operator is running many autonomous agents and needs to read the state of the fleet and commit a decision — approve, deny, defer — the way a pilot reads a gauge and moves a switch: at a glance, under load, with total confidence in what the control does. Every surface is dark so the lit elements carry the eye straight to what needs attention; density is a virtue, because more true information per screen means fewer glances to a decision. The palette is near-black canvas with a single cyan signal color and a three-color status vocabulary borrowed from real instrumentation; type is monospace throughout, sized for a readout, never a headline. It should feel like professional tooling that respects the user's competence and disappears into the task.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, near-black canvas so signal color and status do the wayfinding.
Monospace everywhere; type sized for an instrument readout (11–18px).
One accent (cyan) for action and selection; status carried by a green/red/amber vocabulary.
Flat surfaces built from tonal layering and 1px hairlines — no decorative shadow.
Dense by design: full detail reachable, nothing consequential hidden behind a summary.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: Color is state or action, never decoration. Cyan means 'act here' or 'this is selected'; green/red/amber mean a specific status. If a color isn't telling the operator something true, it doesn't belong on the panel.

rules.name: The Redundant Signal Rule
rules.body: Status is never carried by hue alone. Approve/deny and every status color must be paired with a label, icon, shape, or position so a red/green colorblind operator reads the identical signal.

rules.name: The Instrument-Panel Rule
rules.body: Type is sized for a dense panel, not a landing page. The ceiling is ~22px; nothing shouts. Add hierarchy with weight, color, and spacing before reaching for size.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: One monospace family, full stop. Do not pair it with a sans or serif for contrast — the mono grid is the identity.

rules.name: The Flat-Panel Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. Depth comes from one tonal step and a hairline, never from a blurred shadow.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: No glassmorphism, no decorative backdrop-filter. The only scrim is the modal overlay, and it is a flat dim, not a frosted blur.

dos: Do keep the canvas near-black (#0a0a0a) and let lit elements do the wayfinding.
Do reserve Instrument Cyan for action and current-selection only; treat it as a scarce signal.
Do pair every status color with a label, icon, or shape so approve/deny reads for colorblind operators.
Do size type for a dense instrument panel; add hierarchy with weight, color, and spacing before size, ceiling ~22px.
Do keep surfaces flat — one tonal step (#1a1a1a → #222) plus a hairline (#333) — for depth.
Do expand the full, untruncated detail of any decision in place; a summary is a pointer, never a substitute.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion on every transition, and keep motion at 150–250ms in service of state and feedback only.
Do ship parity of capability across phone-web, desktop-web, and TUI; let the interaction idiom differ, not the power.
donts: Don't make it a rounded, pastel B2B SaaS dashboard — no soft gradients, friendly illustrations, or marketing polish.
Don't make it a gamified notification center — no streaks, engagement badges, confetti, or celebration animation.
Don't perform enterprise security theater — no shields-and-locks iconography or badge-everything compliance aesthetic.
Don't use large, shouty display copy — oversized headings undercut the seriousness and read as consumer marketing.
Don't carry status by hue alone; red-and-green with no label, icon, or shape is forbidden.
Don't add a colored border-left as decoration — the 3px left rail is earned because it encodes session identity; never add another stripe for flavor.
Don't introduce drop shadows, glassmorphism, or decorative backdrop-filter; depth is tonal.
Don't pair the monospace with a second font family for contrast — the mono grid is the identity.
Don't hide the thing being judged behind a truncated summary with no path to the full input.
